Zero-Bloat Architecture: It acts strictly as a configuration engine for native Windows APIs and cmdlets (e.g., Start-MpWDOScan), adding zero ongoing background processing or permanent resource footprints.
Radical Code Transparency: The entire execution logic is delivered via plaintext, fully commented PowerShell scripts, allowing security analysts and system administrators to audit every registry modification, group policy shift, and security toggle prior to deployment.
User-Gated Automation: Critical system interventions—such as initiating an offline boot scan or modifying protection history views—require explicit, interactive confirmation loops to prevent unhandled reboots or loss of volatile user data.
Coexistence with Layered Security: Rather than positioning itself as an exclusive antivirus alternative, it establishes a hardened baseline that complements secondary, specialized remediation tools (like Malwarebytes) by actively detecting their presence and optimizing the overall system posture accordingly.

GatewayGuard is a fully auditable, open-source orchestration layer designed to enforce native Windows 11 Home and Pro security baselines without the overhead, telemetry, or system degradation associated with traditional consumer security suites. By automating the configuration of built-in enterprise-grade protections—such as Memory Integrity (Core Isolation), local access controls, and native backup infrastructure—it replaces opaque third-party software with transparent, verifiable system hardening.
Key Anchors for Technical Reviewers
To secure backing from IT professionals and technical media, the core messaging relies on structural transparency rather than consumer-facing marketing claims:
Zero-Bloat Architecture: It acts strictly as a configuration engine for native Windows APIs and cmdlets (e.g., Start-MpWDOScan), adding zero ongoing background processing or permanent resource footprints.
Radical Code Transparency: The entire execution logic is delivered via plaintext, fully commented PowerShell scripts, allowing security analysts and system administrators to audit every registry modification, group policy shift, and security toggle prior to deployment.
User-Gated Automation: Critical system interventions—such as initiating an offline boot scan or modifying protection history views—require explicit, interactive confirmation loops to prevent unhandled reboots or loss of volatile user data.
Coexistence with Layered Security: Rather than positioning itself as an exclusive antivirus alternative, it establishes a hardened baseline that complements secondary, specialized remediation tools (like Malwarebytes) by actively detecting their presence and optimizing the overall system posture accordingly.
